source.title: Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity 50 years after the Dirac celebrated paper: do unsolved problems still exist?

accepted.question_text: Are Dirac’s Hamiltonian formulation of General Relativity, formulated using the original metric variables, and the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, which reparametrizes gravitational variables using lapse and shift functions together with the spatial three-metric, equivalent Hamiltonian descriptions of the same theory despite the claim that the transformation from the four-metric variables to ADM variables is not canonical in the usual phase space?

evidence.quote: In spite of decades passed from the famous papers by Dirac and ADM, there are unsolved problems. Namely, are the Dirac and ADM formulations equivalent to each other?

the authors claim that the formulation by Dirac and that by ADM are not equivalent since these two formulations are related by a non-canonical transformation of phase space variables from the 4-metrics g_{μν} to the lapse and shift functions N, N_i and the 3-metrics γ_{ij}.
It returns us to the questions: Are the Dirac and ADM formulations really non-equivalent to each other?

accepted.question_text: Are the Hamiltonian formulations of General Relativity associated with Dirac’s original metric-variable approach and the ADM lapse-shift-spatial-metric approach equivalent to original Einstein General Relativity as a Lagrangian theory, rather than being separate Hamiltonian models such as “ADM gravity” with no reference to Einstein General Relativity?

evidence.quote: Are these formulations equivalent to the original (Lagrangian) Einstein theory?
Then, should we consider the ADM formulation as a model named, say, “ADM gravity”, without any reference to Einstein General Relativity, as Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin suggest?

If one used the formalism of extended phase space, the formulation in the ADM variables is expected to be equivalent to the Hamiltonian formulation in terms of metric tensor and conjugate momenta, as well as to the original Einstein General Relativity.

accepted.question_text: Is the group of transformations generated in Hamiltonian phase space the same as, or at least inclusive of, the gauge-transformation group of Einstein General Relativity, including the diffeomorphism-type transformations of all gravitational variables such as g_{0μ} and the ADM lapse and shift variables?
accepted.context_brief: Phase-space transformations versus Einstein gauge transformations

evidence.quote: Is the group of transformation in phase space the same as the group of gauge transformation of the Einstein theory?

The same situation we face in gravitational theory: while the transformations of the 3-metrics can be generated by the secondary (momentum) constraints, the transformation for g_{0μ} cannot be obtained in this way.

In this case the group of transformation in phase space includes the group of gauge transformation of the Einstein theory, and we have an explicit prescription how to build up the generator of these transformations.

accepted.question_text: What principled rules should determine the construction of a generator of gauge transformations in the phase space of constrained gravitational theory, given that constraint-based generator algorithms can depend on the chosen Hamiltonian and parametrization and can give correct transformations only for certain gravitational variables or parametrizations?

evidence.quote: What are rules according to which a generator of transformations in phase space should be constructed?

the rules of constructing the generator are rather artificial and hardly can be recognized as fundamental “rules of procedure” in the sense of Lagrange. We do not even have a strong criterion what exact form a Hamiltonian must take for a constrained theory.
Obviously, the algebra of constraints is not invariant under the choice of parametrization.

Therefore, the derivation of the correct generator requires abandoning the original rules prescribed by Dirac and replacing them by a new procedure presented in [6]. Nevertheless, this new procedure gives right results for a certain parametrization of gravitational variables only.

accepted.question_text: Should the ADM Hamiltonian formulation, or other Hamiltonian formulations based on parametrizations whose canonicity is unproved in the usual phase space, be abandoned or treated as independent models rather than as valid formulations of Einstein General Relativity?
accepted.context_brief: Whether to abandon ADM and other parametrizations

evidence.quote: Should we abandon the ADM formulation because the new ADM variables are not related with the old ones by a canonical transformation? Should we also abandon any other parametrizations if they do not satisfy this criterion?
Then, should we consider the ADM formulation as a model named, say, “ADM gravity”, without any reference to Einstein General Relativity, as Kiriushcheva and Kuzmin suggest?
However, the results are rather indicative, so I cannot see any reason to abandon the ADM parametrization or other possible parametrizations.

accepted.question_text: Does an extended phase-space Hamiltonian formalism, in which gauge degrees of freedom are treated on the same footing as physical degrees of freedom and missing velocities are introduced by differential gauge conditions, provide an alternative to both the original Dirac and ADM approaches while preserving equivalence with the Lagrangian equations and producing correct transformations for all phase variables?
accepted.context_brief: Extended phase space as an alternative Hamiltonian formalism

evidence.quote: Let us mention also another approach based on extended phase space where gauge degrees of freedom are treated on the equal ground with physical degrees of freedom.

Is there an alternative to the both approaches? In Section 4 I shall touch the extended phase space approach that may present such an alternative, and I shall try to answer these questions in Conclusion.
In our extended phase space approach we do not need to abandon generally accepted rules of constructing a Hamiltonian form of the theory or invent some new rules.

the Hamiltonian equations in extended phase space are completely equivalent to the Lagrangian equations; due to global BRST invariance it appears to be possible to construct the BRST charge in conformity with the first Noether theorem which produces correct transformations for all phase variables.

accepted.question_text: Can the results of the extended phase-space approach, which have been demonstrated only for simple models with finitely many degrees of freedom, be reproduced for the full gravitational theory?
accepted.context_brief: Extending simple-model results to full gravity

evidence.quote: Our purpose is to review the above questions and to demonstrate advantages of the extended phase space approach by the example of a simple model with finite number degrees of freedom.
Of course, until now our results have been demonstrated for simple models and it would be important to reproduce them for the full gravitational theory.
